ESV.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
ESV.2: “Can a man be profitable to God? Surely he who is wise is profitable to himself.
ESV.3: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty if you are in the right, or is it gain to him if you make your ways blameless?
ESV.4: Is it for your fear of him that he reproves you and enters into judgment with you?
ESV.5: Is not your evil abundant? There is no end to your iniquities.
ESV.6: For you have exacted pledges of your brothers for nothing and stripped the naked of their clothing.
ESV.7: You have given no water to the weary to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.
ESV.8: The man with power possessed the land, and the favored man lived in it.
ESV.9: You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless were crushed.
ESV.10: Therefore snares are all around you, and sudden terror overwhelms you,
ESV.11: or darkness, so that you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.
ESV.12: “Is not God high in the heavens? See the highest stars, how lofty they are!
ESV.13: But you say, ‘What does God know? Can he judge through the deep darkness?
ESV.14: Thick clouds veil him, so that he does not see, and he walks on the vault of heaven.’
ESV.15: Will you keep to the old way that wicked men have trod?
ESV.16: They were snatched away before their time; their foundation was washed away.
ESV.17: They said to God, ‘Depart from us,’ and ‘What can the Almighty do to us?’
ESV.18: Yet he filled their houses with good things — but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
ESV.19: The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent one mocks at them,
ESV.20: saying, ‘Surely our adversaries are cut off, and what they left the fire has consumed.’
ESV.21: “Agree with God, and be at peace; thereby good will come to you.
ESV.22: Receive instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.
ESV.23: If you return to the Almighty you will be built up; if you remove injustice far from your tents,
ESV.24: if you lay gold in the dust, and gold of Ophir among the stones of the torrent-bed,
ESV.25: then the Almighty will be your gold and your precious silver.
ESV.26: For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
ESV.27: You will make your prayer to him, and he will hear you, and you will pay your vows.
ESV.28: You will decide on a matter, and it will be established for you, and light will shine on your ways.
ESV.29: For when they are humbled you say, ‘It is because of pride’;  but he saves the lowly.
ESV.30: He delivers even the one who is not innocent, who will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”

NLT.2:
“Can a person do anything to help God?
Can even a wise person be helpful to him?
NLT.3:
Is it any advantage to the Almighty if you are righteous?
Would it be any gain to him if you were perfect?
NLT.4:
Is it because you’re so pious that he accuses you
and brings judgment against you?
NLT.5:
No, it’s because of your wickedness!
There’s no limit to your sins.
NLT.6:
“For example, you must have lent money to your friend
and demanded clothing as security.
Yes, you stripped him to the bone.
NLT.7:
You must have refused water for the thirsty
and food for the hungry.
NLT.8:
You probably think the land belongs to the powerful
and only the privileged have a right to it!
NLT.9:
You must have sent widows away empty-handed
and crushed the hopes of orphans.
NLT.10:
That is why you are surrounded by traps
and tremble from sudden fears.
NLT.11:
That is why you cannot see in the darkness,
and waves of water cover you.
NLT.12:
“God is so great — higher than the heavens,
higher than the farthest stars.
NLT.13:
But you reply, ‘That’s why God can’t see what I am doing!
How can he judge through the thick darkness?
NLT.14:
For thick clouds swirl about him, and he cannot see us.
He is way up there, walking on the vault of heaven.’
NLT.15:
“Will you continue on the old paths
where evil people have walked?
NLT.16:
They were snatched away in the prime of life,
the foundations of their lives washed away.
NLT.17:
For they said to God, ‘Leave us alone!
What can the Almighty do to us?’
NLT.18:
Yet he was the one who filled their homes with good things,
so I will have nothing to do with that kind of thinking.
NLT.19:
“The righteous will be happy to see the wicked destroyed,
and the innocent will laugh in contempt.
NLT.20:
They will say, ‘See how our enemies have been destroyed.
The last of them have been consumed in the fire.’
NLT.21:
“Submit to God, and you will have peace;
then things will go well for you.
NLT.22:
Listen to his instructions,
and store them in your heart.
NLT.23:
If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored —
so clean up your life.
NLT.24:
If you give up your lust for money
and throw your precious gold into the river,
NLT.25:
the Almighty himself will be your treasure.
He will be your precious silver!
NLT.26:
“Then you will take delight in the Almighty
and look up to God.
NLT.27:
You will pray to him, and he will hear you,
and you will fulfill your vows to him.
NLT.28:
You will succeed in whatever you choose to do,
and light will shine on the road ahead of you.
NLT.29:
If people are in trouble and you say, ‘Help them,’
God will save them.
NLT.30:
Even sinners will be rescued;
they will be rescued because your hands are pure.”

AMP.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
AMP.2:
"Can a vigorous man be of use to God,
Or a wise man be useful to himself?
AMP.3:
"Is it any pleasure or joy to the Almighty that you are righteous?
Or is it of benefit to Him that you make your ways perfect?
AMP.4:
"Is it because of your fear of Him that He corrects you,
That He enters into judgment against you?
AMP.5:
"Is not your wickedness great,
And your sins without end?
AMP.6:
"For you have taken pledges of your brothers without cause,
And stripped men naked.
AMP.7:
"You have not given water to the weary to drink,
And you have withheld bread from the hungry.
AMP.8:
"But the land is possessed by the man with power,
And the favored and honorable man dwells in it.
AMP.9:
"You have sent widows away empty-handed,
And the arms (strength) of the fatherless have been broken.
AMP.10:
"Therefore snares surround you,
And sudden dread terrifies and overwhelms you;
AMP.11:
Or darkness, so that you cannot see,
And a flood of water covers you.
AMP.12:
"Is not God in the height of heaven?
And behold the distant stars, how high they are!
AMP.13:
"You say, 'What does God know [about me]?
Can He judge through the thick darkness?
AMP.14:
'Thick clouds are a hiding place for Him, so that He cannot see,
And He walks on the vault (circle) of the heavens.'
AMP.15:
"Will you keep to the ancient path
That wicked men walked [in the time of Noah],
AMP.16:
Men who were snatched away before their time,
Whose foundations were poured out like a river?
AMP.17:
"They said to God, 'Depart from us!
What can the Almighty do for us or to us?'
AMP.18:
"Yet He filled their houses with good things;
But the counsel of the wicked and ungodly is far from me.
AMP.19:
"The righteous see it and are glad;
And the innocent mock and laugh at them, saying,
AMP.20:
'Surely our adversaries are cut off and destroyed,
And fire has consumed their abundance.'
AMP.21:
"Now yield and submit yourself to Him [agree with God and be conformed to His will] and be at peace;
In this way [you will prosper and great] good will come to you.
AMP.22:
"Please receive the law and instruction from His mouth
And establish His words in your heart and keep them.
AMP.23:
"If you return to the Almighty [and submit and humble yourself before Him], you will be built up [and restored];
If you remove unrighteousness far from your tents,
AMP.24:
And place your gold in the dust,
And the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks [considering it of little value],
AMP.25:
And make the Almighty your gold
And your precious silver,
AMP.26:
Then you will have delight in the Almighty,
And you will lift up your face to God.
AMP.27:
"You will pray to Him, and He will hear you,
And you will pay your vows.
AMP.28:
"You will also decide and decree a thing, and it will be established for you;
And the light [of God's favor] will shine upon your ways.
AMP.29:
"When you are cast down and humbled, you will speak with confidence,
And the humble person He will lift up and save.
AMP.30:
"He will even rescue the one [for whom you intercede] who is not innocent;
And he will be rescued through the cleanness of your hands."

WEB.2: “Can a man be profitable to God? Surely he who is wise is profitable to himself.
WEB.3: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that you are righteous? Or does it benefit him, that you make your ways perfect?
WEB.4: Is it for your piety that he reproves you, that he enters with you into judgment?
WEB.5: Isn’t your wickedness great? Neither is there any end to your iniquities.
WEB.6: For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
WEB.7: You haven’t given water to the weary to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.
WEB.8: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.
WEB.9: You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
WEB.10: Therefore snares are around you. Sudden fear troubles you,
WEB.11: or darkness, so that you can not see, and floods of waters cover you.

WEB.21: “Acquaint yourself with him, now, and be at peace. Thereby good shall come to you.

WEB.23: If you return to the Almighty, you shall be built up, if you put away unrighteousness far from your tents.
WEB.24: Lay your treasure in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks.
WEB.25: The Almighty will be your treasure, and precious silver to you.
WEB.26: For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and shall lift up your face to God.
WEB.27: You shall make your prayer to him, and he will hear you. You shall pay your vows.
WEB.28: You shall also decree a thing, and it shall be established to you. Light shall shine on your ways.
WEB.29: When they cast down, you shall say, ‘be lifted up.’ He will save the humble person.
WEB.30: He will even deliver him who is not innocent. Yes, he shall be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”

MSG.1: Once again Eliphaz the Temanite took up his theme:
MSG.2:
"Are any of us strong enough to give God a hand,
or smart enough to give him advice?
MSG.3:
So what if you were righteous—would God Almighty even notice?
Even if you gave a perfect performance, do you think
he'd applaud?
MSG.4:
Do you think it's because he cares about your purity
that he's disciplining you, putting you on the spot?
MSG.5:
Hardly! It's because you're a first-class moral failure,
because there's no end to your sins.
MSG.6:
When people came to you for help,
you took the shirts off their backs, exploited their helplessness.
MSG.7:
You wouldn't so much as give a drink to the thirsty,
or food, not even a scrap, to the hungry.
MSG.8:
And there you sat, strong and honored by everyone,
surrounded by immense wealth!
MSG.9:
You turned poor widows away from your door;
heartless, you crushed orphans.
MSG.10:
Now you're the one trapped in terror, paralyzed by fear.
Suddenly the tables have turned!
MSG.11:
How do you like living in the dark, sightless,
up to your neck in flood waters?
MSG.12:
"You agree, don't you, that God is in charge?
He runs the universe—just look at the stars!
MSG.13:
Yet you dare raise questions: 'What does God know?
From that distance and darkness, how can he judge?
MSG.14:
He roams the heavens wrapped in clouds,
so how can he see us?'
MSG.15:
"Are you going to persist in that tired old line
that wicked men and women have always used?
MSG.16:
Where did it get them? They died young,
flash floods sweeping them off to their doom.
MSG.17:
They told God, 'Get lost!
What good is God Almighty to us?'
MSG.18:
And yet it was God who gave them everything they had.
It's beyond me how they can carry on like this!
MSG.19:
"Good people see bad people crash, and call for a celebration.
Relieved, they crow,
MSG.20:
'At last! Our enemies—wiped out.
Everything they had and stood for is up in smoke!'
MSG.21:
"Give in to God, come to terms with him
and everything will turn out just fine.
MSG.22:
Let him tell you what to do;
take his words to heart.
MSG.23:
Come back to God Almighty
and he'll rebuild your life.
Clean house of everything evil.
MSG.24:
Relax your grip on your money
and abandon your gold-plated luxury.
MSG.25:
God Almighty will be your treasure,
more wealth than you can imagine.
MSG.26:
"You'll take delight in God, the Mighty One,
and look to him joyfully, boldly.
MSG.27:
You'll pray to him and he'll listen;
he'll help you do what you've promised.
MSG.28:
You'll decide what you want and it will happen;
your life will be bathed in light.
MSG.29:
To those who feel low you'll say, 'Chin up! Be brave!'
and God will save them.
MSG.30:
Yes, even the guilty will escape,
escape through God's grace in your life."

NRSVCE.4:

NRSVCE.5:
Is not your wickedness great?

NRSVCE.8:

and the favored live in it.
NRSVCE.9:
You have sent widows away empty-handed,
and the arms of the orphans you have crushed.
NRSVCE.10:
Therefore snares are around you,
and sudden terror overwhelms you,

NRSVCE.15:
Will you keep to the old way
that the wicked have trod?

NRSVCE.17:

If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored,

NET.2: “Is it to God that a strong man is of benefit? Is it to him that even a wise man is profitable?
NET.3: Is it of any special benefit to the Almighty that you should be righteous, or is it any gain to him that you make your ways blameless?
NET.4: Is it because of your piety that he rebukes you and goes to judgment with you?
NET.5: Is not your wickedness great and is there no end to your iniquity?
NET.6: “For you took pledges from your brothers for no reason, and you stripped the clothing from the naked.
NET.7: You gave the weary no water to drink and from the hungry you withheld food.
NET.8: Although you were a powerful man, owning land, an honored man living on it,
NET.9: you sent widows away empty-handed, and the arms of the orphans you crushed.
NET.10: That is why snares surround you, and why sudden fear terrifies you,
NET.11: why it is so dark you cannot see, and why a flood of water covers you.
NET.12: “Is not God on high in heaven? And see the lofty stars, how high they are!
NET.13: But you have said, ‘What does God know? Does he judge through such deep darkness?
NET.14: Thick clouds are a veil for him, so he does not see us, as he goes back and forth in the vault of heaven.’
NET.15: Will you keep to the old path that evil men have walked —
NET.16: men who were carried off before their time, when the flood was poured out on their foundations?
NET.17: They were saying to God, ‘Turn away from us,’ and ‘What can the Almighty do to us?’
NET.18: But it was he who filled their houses with good things — yet the counsel of the wicked was far from me.
NET.19: The righteous see their destruction and rejoice; the innocent mock them scornfully, saying,
NET.20: ‘Surely our enemies are destroyed, and fire consumes their wealth.’
NET.21: “Reconcile yourself with God, and be at peace with him; in this way your prosperity will be good.
NET.22: Accept instruction from his mouth and store up his words in your heart.
NET.23: If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up; if you remove wicked behavior far from your tent,
NET.24: and throw your gold in the dust — your gold of Ophir among the rocks in the ravines —
NET.25: then the Almighty himself will be your gold, and the choicest silver for you.
NET.26: Surely then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and will lift up your face toward God.
NET.27: You will pray to him and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows to him.
NET.28: Whatever you decide on a matter, it will be established for you, and light will shine on your ways.
NET.29: When people are brought low and you say ‘Lift them up!’ then he will save the downcast;
NET.30: he will deliver even someone who is not innocent, who will escape through the cleanness of your hands.”
